item.description:
### Performance - **Perch uses about a quarter of the CPU it did while agents work.** A working fleet idled Perch at 12–16% of a core; the same workload now sits around 3%. Four things changed: a burst of agent activity now redraws the fleet once instead of once per event; reading whether a Claude turn was interrupted no longer re-reads a quarter-megabyte of transcript on every redraw; the menu bar label only re-renders when something it actually shows changes; and a long Codex turn no longer rescans megabytes of its own history every four seconds. Nothing you see changes — the Mac just does less to show it.
### Changed - **Perch does much less work while Claude's status line refreshes.** Claude Code redraws its status line every few seconds per session, and Perch's helper rewrites four small files each time. Those files lived next to the session records, so every refresh made Perch re-read the whole records directory and redraw the menu bar. They now live in their own folder (`…/Perch/aggregate/`, moved automatically on first launch) with their own watcher, and unchanged numbers no longer trigger a redraw. Nothing you see changes.
### Fixed - **Perch tells you when its icon is hidden.** On a MacBook with a notch and a full menu bar, macOS puts a new icon straight behind the notch, so a fresh install could be running with nothing on screen and no hint that it was. Perch now notices and sends one notification saying so, with the shortcut that opens the fleet window (⌃⌥⌘P). Clicking the notification opens it too. At most one notice a week, so if you tucked the icon away on purpose it will not keep telling you. - **The fleet says when it is not current.** When your Mac sleeps, every agent pauses with it, but the panel kept showing the last thing it saw as if it were live. Perch now shows one line as the Mac goes to sleep, one while it re-checks after waking ("Back from 25 min asleep — refreshing"), and one if checks stop landing for any other reason ("Last checked 3 min ago — this may be out of date"). Nothing is shown while everything is normal. On waking, Perch re-scans immediately and sends the result to your phone, rather than waiting for the next timer. - **Your phone and watch know when the Mac is asleep.** They used to show "Reconnecting…" with a spinner for the whole nap. Now the Mac tells them as it goes to sleep, and they say "Mac went to sleep 22 min ago — the fleet is paused" instead, and "Mac just woke — refreshing" when it comes back. While reconnecting for any other reason, they say how old what you are looking at is. The lock-screen card also dims within two minutes of the Mac sleeping rather than looking current for up to an hour. Needs the iPhone app 1.0.2.
